pre_result_plan.real_task: Generate the required connector publication manifest before remote writes using the CLI's revision selectors.
pre_result_plan.observed_problem: Session 057 repeated Session 042's natural failure by using --base-ref/--target-ref; both calls returned invalid_arguments and needed one retry with --base/--commit.
pre_result_plan.baseline: The observed Session 057 task had 1 failed manifest invocation before the valid manifest; Session 042 independently had the same failure shape.
pre_result_plan.hypothesis: Supporting exactly the twice-observed --base-ref and --target-ref aliases will make the recorded failed invocation succeed with the same manifest as canonical syntax, reducing failed invocations in replay from 1 to 0.
pre_result_plan.metric: failed manifest invocations before a valid manifest
pre_result_plan.quality_control: Alias and canonical forms must emit byte-identical JSON for the same revisions; existing required-argument and Git validation behavior must remain green.
pre_result_plan.overhead: Count design, code, tests, replay, evidence, documentation, checkpoint maintenance and publication; replay cannot prove future field utility.
pre_result_plan.stop_condition: Reject the aliases if they require semantic changes beyond argparse names, conflict with canonical flags, or do not reproduce the canonical manifest exactly.

result.reason: Two argparse aliases absorb the twice-observed naming mistake while preserving one implementation path and canonical output; no wrapper, pre-read mandate or fallback parser is justified.
limitations: The intervention is a replay of the real Session 057 command after implementation, not a prospective field use.
The two natural failures were made by the same Agent 1 across different sessions, so this does not establish transfer to other agents.
